sections.content: How many people are "electrical and electronic trades (other)"?

28,260 people

were counted on the census as "electrical and electronic trades (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.
People who do this type of work carry out a variety of electrical and electronic occupations not elsewhere classified.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "electrical and electronic trades (other)" there were more men than women (93.6% compared with 6.4%).

This means "electrical and electronic trades (other)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled metal, electrical and electronic trades".

Men made up 93.6% and women made up 6.4% of "electrical and electronic trades (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "electrical and electronic trades (other)" included:

  • telecoms and related network installers and repairers
  • pest control officers
  • street cleaners

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "electrical and electronic trades (other)" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "electrical and electronic trades (other)", 13.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "electrical and electronic trades (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "electrical and electronic trades (other)" included:

  • welfare and housing associate professionals (other)
  • estimators, valuers and assessors
  • electronics engineers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "electrical and electronic trades (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "electrical and electronic trades (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "electrical and electronic trades (other)", 7.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (93.2% compared with 6.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (92%) than self-employed (8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
